summary: Read-only review complete: 3 findings. No edits, builds, tests, or network access.

findings.title: TOTP re-enrollment can retain or restore obsolete step-up authority
findings.detail: Clearing step_up_at only on disable does not bind subsequent step-up authority to the enrolled factor. Sequence: disable TOTP, obtain password-only step-up while totp_secret is NULL, then re-enable TOTP on the same session. packages/api/src/routes/admin-system.ts:169-180 permits that password-only proof; packages/api/src/auth/admin-staff.ts:104-107 preserves the calling session and its step_up_at on enable. Registration then accepts the timestamp without proof of the new factor. Additionally, an in-flight native step-up can write its timestamp after recovery because markStepUpVerified performs no credential snapshot recheck. This affects the previous-image rollback guarantee too.
findings.fix: Invalidate step-up authority durably on enrollment as well as disable, and make native step-up commit under the owner lock with credential snapshot and session revalidation. Define a rollback-safe treatment of retained sessions that also prevents late previous-image step-up writes. Cover both the sequential password-only case and an in-flight step-up crossing recovery.

findings.title: Revoking other sessions preserves the customer/session deadlock cycle
findings.detail: Removing SELECT FOR UPDATE from session validation does not eliminate session locks: DELETE acquires them too. A profile request using session B can renew B and hold its row lock, then wait for the customer locked by password change through session A. Password change subsequently deletes B and waits for the profile transaction. packages/api/src/auth/session.ts:147-151 performs the renewal; packages/api/src/routes/account.ts:353-360 updates the customer afterward; account.ts:389-393 supplies the session deletion retained by this design. Address insertion at account.ts:415-424 can similarly wait on the customer through its FK. PostgreSQL must abort one transaction, contradicting the stated lock-order guarantee.
findings.fix: Make the affected profile/address paths acquire the customer lock before renewing or otherwise locking sessions, or move their renewal outside the transaction that touches the customer. Add deterministic two-session controls racing these routes against the restructured password change, including its actual session deletion.

findings.title: Pending mailbox tokens survive passkey deletion and can recreate grants
findings.detail: Mailbox proof is stored separately as customer_token(kind='passkey_manage'), but deletion invalidates challenges and grants without explicitly invalidating these pending tokens. Branch D confirmation checks the unchanged password fingerprint, session and nonce; it does not recheck the no-passkey condition. An attacker retaining an unused mailbox token and its bound session/nonce from before enrollment can redeem it after a compromised passkey is removed, obtain a fresh grant and register another credential. packages/api/src/db/schema-content.ts:19-30 confirms customer_token has no credential linkage or cascade; packages/api/src/routes/customer-tokens.ts:137-145 demonstrates that token invalidation requires explicit updates by kind. Deleting customer_passkey_challenge rows cannot revoke this authorization source.
findings.fix: Explicitly invalidate unused passkey_manage customer_token rows under the customer lock whenever pending management authorization is revoked, including passkey deletion. Recheck mailbox-bootstrap eligibility at confirmation and cover request-token issuance followed by enrollment, credential deletion, and attempted confirmation with the original session and nonce.
